label: node removal
type: flagging a node for removal from the cluster so that the following rebalance recreates its replica vBuckets on the remaining nodes before the node leaves. Unlike failover, a node does not have to be failed over before being removed - and unlike failover, no replicas are lost.
evidence: When a node is flagged for _removal_ (as opposed to _failover_), new replica vBuckets will be created on the remaining nodes, as node-removal proceeds.
A node can be removed from the cluster by means of the CLI. Note that the node does not have to be _failed over_ prior to removal.
By contrast, _removal_ creates new copies of replica vBuckets that would otherwise be lost (thereby creating greater competition for the memory resources of the surviving nodes).
note: Also the mechanism behind an operation that looks unrelated: manage-data-service-and-rebalance.md instructs an administrator to add the Data Service to an existing node by REMOVING the node and adding it back. Round 26 found four distinct procedures (add, join, remove, modify-services) whose only stated completion condition is a rebalance, which is what makes rebalance the hub of this subtree rather than one operation among many.
